Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

This conversation uses two-stage tool calling. First, call exactly the meta-tool below; do not call a real tool before the tool response arrives. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

Meta-tool schema:
{
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "select_tool",
    "description": "Choose the one real tool that should handle the query.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "tool_name": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "get_all_list",
            "NewsProvider.getAllFootballTransferNews",
            "get_all_the_top_350_cryptocurrency_exchange_rates_and_prices",
            "api.get_last_cryptocurrency_news",

            "farfetch_lookup_by_product_id"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "tool_name"
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}

I've been hearing my grandson talk about something called 'cryptocurrencies' while he's been visiting. Now, I don't pretend to understand all that digital money business, but I figure I should at least know what the fuss is about. Could you start by giving me the latest general news and updates on the whole crypto market? If there's any significant news about a specific cryptocurrency, like Bitcoin or Ethereum—those names I've heard mentioned—then maybe dig into that one a bit deeper. I'd like to know what's making waves out there, even if I'm still partial to good old cash in my wallet.

offset.description: Offset for pagination. Defaults to 0.

region.description: Region code for filtering categories. Defaults to 'US'.

normalized_functions.name: leagues
normalized_functions.description: Retrieves a list of sports leagues using the provided RapidAPI key. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

lang.description: Language code for the response (e.g., 'en' for English).

normalized_functions.name: exchange_currency

tocurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the target currency (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Must be uppercase letters.

fromcurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the source currency (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Must be uppercase letters.

amount.description: Numeric value to convert, provided as a string to maintain precision (e.g., '150.25').

normalized_functions.name: usd_egp

date.description: Date string in YYYY-MM-DD format for historical exchange rate lookup. Defaults to current date if not specified.

decimal_places.description: Number of decimal places to format the converted EGP amount. Valid values: 0-6. Default is 2.

normalized_functions.name: get_list_of_news

page.description: The page number to retrieve. Must be an integer greater than or equal to 1. Defaults to 1 when not provided.

tag.description: Filter news articles by a specific tag or keyword. Mutually exclusive with the 'category' parameter.

codigomoeda.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the target currency (e.g., USD for US Dollar, EUR for Euro). Case-sensitive and must be uppercase.

normalized_functions.name: extract_content

moeda.description: Currency pair in {source}-{target} format (e.g., USD-BRL, EUR-BRL). Must be a supported exchange pair

normalized_functions.name: getrandomword

securityid.description: The security ID obtained from the .../market/v2/get-returns endpoint.

duration.description: The time duration for the returns. Must be one of 'daily', 'monthly', or 'quarterly'. Defaults to 'daily'.

This conversation uses two-stage tool calling. First, call exactly the meta-tool below; do not call a real tool before the tool response arrives. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

{

  "function": {

    "description": "Choose the one real tool that should handle the query.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "tool_name": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [

            "converter",
            "leagues",

            "get_stores",

      },
      "required": [
        "tool_name"
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}
